commands.step: Install (npm ci, from the committed lockfile)
Run tests (ubuntu/20 — records the pass count)
commands.text:
set -euo pipefail
# Full treatment Phase 4b: coverage rides on the cell that ALREADY
# runs the suite for the count parser — `test:coverage` is
# `vitest run --coverage`, the same single run, so this adds no
# second full-suite execution (the standing CI-minute rule). The
# count parser below was verified against coverage output before
# this swap: the `Tests N passed` line is unchanged.
npm run test:coverage 2>&1 | tee test-output.txt
CLEAN="$(sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' test-output.txt)"
PASSED="$(printf '%s\n' "$CLEAN" | grep -E "^\s*Tests\s+" | tail -1 | sed -E 's/.*\b([0-9]+)\s+passed.*/\1/' || true)"
if [ -z "$PASSED" ]; then
  echo "::error::Could not parse passing-test count from vitest output."
  exit 1
fi
echo "Resolved passing test count: $PASSED"
echo "passed=$PASSED" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

commands.step: Install (npm ci, from the committed lockfile)
npm ci against the committed lockfile (fails on desync)
Tool docs match a fresh docgen (schema change without regen fails)
Pack the tarball a user would install
commands.text:
set -euo pipefail
# --ignore-scripts: `prepack` is `clean && build`, which would wipe
# the dist/ the previous two steps just produced and verified. The
# tarball listing does not require prepack to run; tests/pack.test.ts
# skips it for the same reason.
TGZ="$(npm pack --ignore-scripts --silent | tail -n 1)"
# Guard the --silent contract: if a future npm stops printing the
# filename on stdout, fail here rather than mv-ing a bogus name.
if [ -z "$TGZ" ] || [ ! -f "$TGZ" ]; then
  echo "::error::npm pack --silent did not name a tarball (got: '$TGZ')"
  exit 1
fi
mv "$TGZ" "$RUNNER_TEMP/$TGZ"
echo "tarball=$RUNNER_TEMP/$TGZ" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "packed $TGZ into $RUNNER_TEMP"

commands.step: Install the tarball and run the binary (no Ollama, no API key)
commands.text:
set -euo pipefail

# The whole point of this gate is the no-key path. A secret mapped
# into this job later would silently turn it into a cloud test.
if [ -n "${OLLAMA_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
  echo "::error::OLLAMA_API_KEY is set in this job — the tarball smoke must prove the zero-egress, no-key path. Put cloud assertions in cloud-smoke instead."
  exit 1
fi

SMOKE="$RUNNER_TEMP/tarball-smoke"
rm -rf "$SMOKE"
mkdir -p "$SMOKE/install" "$SMOKE/cwd"
# Keep doctor's log lookup out of the runner's home dir.
export INTERN_LOG_PATH="$SMOKE/log.ndjson"

# Install what `npm i ollama-intern-mcp` installs: the packed tarball
# plus its runtime deps, resolved fresh from the registry.
cd "$SMOKE/install"
npm init -y >/dev/null 2>&1
npm i --no-audit --no-fund --loglevel=error "$TARBALL"

# Through the bin shim, not `node dist/index.js` — the shim is what
# proves package.json `bin` mapped and dist/index.js kept its shebang.
BIN="$SMOKE/install/node_modules/.bin/ollama-intern-mcp"
if [ ! -x "$BIN" ]; then
  echo "::error::bin shim missing or not executable at $BIN — package.json \"bin\" did not install."
  exit 1
fi

# 1. --version: it starts, and it agrees with the manifest it shipped from.
WANT="$(node -p "require('$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/package.json').version")"
GOT="$("$BIN" --version)"
echo "--version: $GOT (manifest says $WANT)"
if [ "$GOT" != "$WANT" ]; then
  echo "::error::installed binary reports $GOT but package.json says $WANT"
  exit 1
fi

# 2. --help: still advertises the verbs it advertises. `init` is
#    listed here, which is what makes step 4 a contract and not a
#    nice-to-have.
"$BIN" --help > "$SMOKE/help.txt"
for verb in init doctor; do
  if ! grep -qE "^[[:space:]]+$verb[[:space:]]" "$SMOKE/help.txt"; then
    echo "::error::--help no longer lists the $verb verb"
    exit 1
  fi
done
echo "--help: lists init + doctor"

# 3. doctor --json: exit 0 and a parseable envelope. NOT healthy —
#    there is no Ollama here, and this deliberately does not pass
#    --fail-unhealthy.
"$BIN" doctor --json > "$SMOKE/doctor.json"
node -e '
  const fs = require("node:fs");
  const d = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8"));
  for (const k of ["healthy", "profile", "ollama", "models", "paths", "warnings"]) {
    if (!(k in d)) {
      console.error("::error::doctor --json is missing the \"" + k + "\" key");
      process.exit(1);
    }
  }
  if (d.ollama.reachable !== false) {
    console.error("::error::doctor reports a reachable Ollama on a runner that has none — OLLAMA_HOST did not take effect, so this run proved nothing about the offline path");
    process.exit(1);
  }
  console.log("doctor --json: ok (healthy=" + d.healthy + ", reachable=" + d.ollama.reachable + ", warnings=" + d.warnings.length + ")");
' "$SMOKE/doctor.json"

# 4. init: the assertion this gate exists for. It copies
#    hermes.config.example.yaml out of the installed package root, so
#    it goes red the moment that file stops shipping — the exact
#    defect a file-list test cannot see.
cd "$SMOKE/cwd"
if ! "$BIN" init; then
  echo "::error::\`init\` failed from a real npm install. If it printed \"example config not found\", then hermes.config.example.yaml is missing from package.json \`files\` — that is exactly the defect this gate exists for (F-c32cff48); a file-list test cannot see it."
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s hermes.config.yaml ]; then
  echo "::error::init exited 0 but wrote no hermes.config.yaml"
  exit 1
fi
echo "init: wrote $(wc -c < hermes.config.yaml) bytes of hermes.config.yaml"

echo "tarball smoke: OK — the published artifact installs and runs."

commands.step: Install (npm ci, from the committed lockfile)

commands.text:
set -euo pipefail
if [ -z "${OLLAMA_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
  echo "::notice::OLLAMA_CLOUD secret not set (fork or unconfigured repo) — skipping cloud smoke test."
  exit 0
fi
# doctor exits 0 even when unhealthy (its job is to REPORT). Capture
# the human-readable report and assert the Cloud (primary) block.
node dist/index.js doctor | tee doctor.out
echo "----------------------------------------"
if ! grep -q "Cloud (primary):" doctor.out; then
  echo "::error::doctor output is missing the 'Cloud (primary)' block — cloud config was not loaded."
  exit 1
fi
# Extract just the Cloud block (header → next blank line) so we don't
# accidentally match the local Ollama block's own 'reachable:' line.
cloud_block="$(awk '/^Cloud \(primary\):/{f=1} f{print} /^$/{if(f)exit}' doctor.out)"
echo "--- Cloud (primary) block ---"
echo "$cloud_block"
if ! echo "$cloud_block" | grep -q "reachable: yes"; then
  echo "::error::Cloud (primary) block does not report 'reachable: yes' — cloud host did not answer."
  exit 1
fi
echo "cloud-smoke (doctor): OK — Ollama Cloud is reachable."

set -euo pipefail
if [ -z "${OLLAMA_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
  echo "::notice::OLLAMA_CLOUD secret not set — skipping real cloud generate."
  exit 0
fi
node scripts/cloud-smoke-generate.mjs

commands.step: Check CHANGELOG entry exists for current version
commands.text:
if ! grep -F -- "## [$VERSION]" CHANGELOG.md > /dev/null; then
  echo "::error file=CHANGELOG.md::No CHANGELOG entry found for version ${VERSION}. Expected a heading like '## [${VERSION}] — YYYY-MM-DD'."
  echo ""
  echo "Most recent CHANGELOG headings:"
  grep -E "^## " CHANGELOG.md | head -5 || true
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok — CHANGELOG entry found for v${VERSION}"

commands.step: Check release notes do not contain TBD dates
commands.text:
if [ ! -d docs/release-notes ]; then
  echo "ok — no docs/release-notes/ directory"
  exit 0
fi
# Match 'Released: TBD' or 'Released:**TBD' or 'TBD' alone on a date line
if grep -RnE "Released:\s*\*?\*?\s*TBD" docs/release-notes/; then
  echo "::error::Found 'Released: TBD' in docs/release-notes/. Replace with the actual release date before merge."
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok — no TBD dates in release notes"

commands.step: Check README/HANDOFF test count matches TEST_COUNT marker
commands.text:
if [ ! -f HANDOFF.md ]; then
  echo "::error file=HANDOFF.md::HANDOFF.md missing; cannot resolve TEST_COUNT marker."
  exit 1
fi
ACTUAL="$(grep -oE '<!-- TEST_COUNT:start -->[0-9]+<!-- TEST_COUNT:end -->' HANDOFF.md | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)"
if [ -z "$ACTUAL" ]; then
  echo "::error file=HANDOFF.md::Could not parse TEST_COUNT marker."
  exit 1
fi
echo "Resolved TEST_COUNT marker: $ACTUAL"
DRIFT=0

# README: look for "<N> tests" or "<N> passing" near the badge / header.
# We only scan files that are likely to make a load-bearing claim.
for file in README.md HANDOFF.md SHIP_GATE.md; do
  if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then continue; fi
  # Match patterns like '792 tests', '792 passing', 'Tests: 792'.
  STATED="$(grep -oE '[0-9]{2,5}\s+(tests|passing)|Tests:\s*[0-9]{2,5}|tests:\s*[0-9]{2,5}' "$file" | head -3 || true)"
  if [ -z "$STATED" ]; then continue; fi
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    NUM="$(echo "$line" | grep -oE '[0-9]+')"
    if [ -z "$NUM" ]; then continue; fi
    if [ "$NUM" != "$ACTUAL" ]; then
      echo "::error file=$file::Stated test count '$line' (parsed: $NUM) does not match TEST_COUNT marker ($ACTUAL). Run 'npm run sync-docs' to refresh."
      DRIFT=1
    fi
  done <<< "$STATED"
done

if [ "$DRIFT" -ne 0 ]; then
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok — stated test counts match TEST_COUNT marker ($ACTUAL)"

COUNT="$(grep -oE '<!-- TEST_COUNT:start -->[0-9]+<!-- TEST_COUNT:end -->' HANDOFF.md | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)"
if [ -z "$COUNT" ]; then
  echo "::error file=HANDOFF.md::Could not parse TEST_COUNT marker for sync-docs:check."
  exit 1
fi
node scripts/sync-doc-versions.mjs --check --test-count="$COUNT"

if [ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" = "tag" ]; then
  VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
else
  VERSION=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
fi
echo "version=${VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "tag=v${VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

PKG="v$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"
if [ "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" != "$PKG" ]; then
  echo "::error::Tag ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} does not match package.json $PKG"
  exit 1
fi

commands.step: Install npm >=11.5 for OIDC trusted publishing
commands.text:
SANDBOX="$HOME/.npm-cli-sandbox"
mkdir -p "$SANDBOX"
( cd "$SANDBOX" \
  && echo '{"name":"npm-cli-sandbox","version":"0.0.0","private":true}' > package.json \
  && npm install --no-save --no-audit --no-fund --silent npm@latest )
echo "$SANDBOX/node_modules/.bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
"$SANDBOX/node_modules/.bin/npm" --version

NAME=$(node -p "require('./package.json').name")
VER=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
if npm view "$NAME@$VER" version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "skip $NAME@$VER (already published)"
else
  npm publish --provenance --access public
fi

VERSION="${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }}"
SECTION=$(awk -v ver="$VERSION" '
  $0 ~ "^## \\[?" ver "\\]?" { found=1; next }
  found && /^## / { exit }
  found { print }
' CHANGELOG.md)
if [ -z "$SECTION" ]; then
  echo "::warning::No CHANGELOG section for v${VERSION}; falling back to auto-notes"
  echo "has_section=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
else
  printf "%s\n" "$SECTION" > .release-notes.md
  echo "has_section=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi

TAG="${{ steps.ver.outputs.tag }}"
if gh release view "$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Release $TAG already exists; skipping create."
elif [ "${{ steps.changelog.outputs.has_section }}" = "true" ]; then
  gh release create "$TAG" --title "$TAG" --notes-file .release-notes.md --verify-tag
else
  gh release create "$TAG" --title "$TAG" --generate-notes --verify-tag
fi
